newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Tokyo Electron aims to boost share price.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Tokyo Electron aims to boost share price.

text.p: The president of Tokyo Electron Ltd, a manufacturer of chip production equipment, said he hopes to boost the company's share price to a level of around 7,000-8,000 yen in the year 2000.
"I'm aiming to raise the share price (of the company) to the 7,000 to 8,000 level in 2000," Tetsuro Higashi told Reuters in a recent interview.
The company's shares ended down 210 yen at 5,460 yen on Friday.
Tokyo Electron recently introduced a unique incentive plan for its executives instead of offering a stock-option programme as many companies have done.
Under the firm's incentive plan, compensation is based on several criteria, including the company's profit growth rate and group-based return-on-equity.
Higashi said the incentive plan is in the interest of shareholders, because it will strengthen the company's business which will then result in a higher share price.

The company forecasts a group current profit of 52 billion yen in the current fiscal year to March 1998, down 4.5 percent from the previous year. However, Higashi said the company is likely to revise its forecast upwards later this year when demand in the summer and early autumn becomes clearer.
He said company orders have recovered since hitting bottom in the July-September period of 1996.
"The biggest reason for the recovery is that semiconductor manufacturers are making investments in 64 megabit DRAMs (dynamic random access memories) and embedded DRAMs in advance," Higashi said.
Embedded DRAMs integrate traditional DRAMs with digital logic on a single chip.
The company president also said sales in the United States are expected to almost double in the current business year to 56 billion yen from 28.7 billion yen last year.
He said he wants to raise the proportion of U.S. sales to total more than 20 percent from eight percent in 1996/97.
He also said that the liquid crystal display (LCD) business is expected to turn profitable this business year as there will be fewer costs related to initial investment.
LCD sales are likely to increase 54 percent from the previous year to 27 billion yen in 1997/98 and jump more than 250 percent in the next three years, he said.
Higashi said he does not plan to finance the 38-billion-yen group capital investment planned for 1997/98 through a new share issue.
